product_overview: Gardiyan2 is an Android app that helps users set daily time limits for selected applications and automatically blocks them when the limit is reached. It relies on accessibility, usage stats, overlay, and related Android permissions to monitor app usage and enforce restrictions.
core_goals: Allow users to define and manage daily usage limits for selected apps.
Detect when a restricted app becomes active in the foreground.
Block access to restricted apps with a system overlay once the daily limit is reached.
Verify and request required Android permissions for monitoring and enforcement.
Persist critical events and restriction changes for traceability.
Provide a hardened unlocking mechanism to prevent accidental or unauthorized disabling of protection.

features.name: Restricted App Management
features.description: Users can add, update, and remove app packages that should be subject to daily time limits.
user_flows: GET /api/restrictions to retrieve the current list of restricted apps -> Receive 200 with the saved restriction list -> POST /api/restrictions with a new package and daily limit -> Receive 201 confirming the restriction was saved -> GET /api/restrictions to verify the new app appears in the list
POST /api/restrictions with an invalid or empty package name -> Receive 400 with a validation error -> GET /api/restrictions to confirm the list was not changed

PUT /api/restrictions/{packageName} with a new daily limit -> Receive 200 confirming the restriction was updated -> DELETE /api/restrictions/{packageName} to remove the app -> Receive 200 confirming the restriction was deleted

features.name: App Usage Monitoring
features.description: The app monitors foreground usage to determine whether a restricted application is currently active and track daily usage against the configured limit.
user_flows: GET /api/usage/current for the active foreground app -> Receive 200 with the current package name and usage state -> GET /api/restrictions/{packageName} to confirm the app is restricted -> Receive 200 with the restriction details
GET /api/usage/current when usage stats or accessibility access is missing -> Receive 403 indicating monitoring is unavailable until permission is granted
GET /api/usage/current for a restricted app that is not currently in the foreground -> Receive 200 showing no active restricted app and no block trigger

features.name: Blocking Overlay Screen
features.description: When a restricted app exceeds its daily allowance, the app displays a blocking overlay that prevents further use until the user unlocks it.
user_flows: POST /api/blocking/check with the current package and usage totals -> Receive 200 indicating the limit has been reached -> POST /api/blocking/show to display the overlay -> Receive 200 confirming the overlay is active -> GET /api/blocking/status to verify the app is blocked
POST /api/blocking/check with usage below the configured daily limit -> Receive 200 indicating no block is needed -> GET /api/blocking/status to confirm the overlay remains inactive
POST /api/blocking/show without overlay permission granted -> Receive 403 with a permission error -> GET /api/permissions/overlay to verify overlay permission is still missing

features.name: Persistent Logging
features.description: The app records important actions and security-related events such as permission changes, restriction updates, and overlay behavior.
user_flows: POST /api/logs with a permission-granted or restriction-changed event -> Receive 201 confirming the event was stored -> GET /api/logs to retrieve recent log entries -> Receive 200 with the persisted history
POST /api/logs with malformed event data -> Receive 400 with a validation error -> GET /api/logs to confirm no invalid entry was added
GET /api/logs to audit overlay show/hide activity after a blocking event -> Receive 200 with matching event records

features.name: Permissions Verification
features.description: Users must grant and verify essential Android permissions including overlay, usage stats, accessibility, notifications, and battery optimization exemptions.
user_flows: GET /api/permissions to retrieve the current permission status set -> Receive 200 with overlay, usage stats, accessibility, notification, and battery optimization states -> POST /api/permissions/request to trigger the required permission flow -> Receive 200 or 202 confirming the request was started

POST /api/permissions/request when a permission is permanently denied -> Receive 409 or 403 indicating the permission cannot be requested normally -> GET /api/permissions to confirm the denied state remains unchanged

GET /api/permissions/overlay, GET /api/permissions/usage-stats, and GET /api/permissions/accessibility to verify each critical permission individually -> Receive 200 for granted permissions or 403 for missing permissions

features.name: Hardened Unblocking
features.description: To disable monitoring or unlock restricted apps, the user must perform a protected five-second long press action to prevent accidental or unauthorized unblocking.
user_flows: POST /api/unblock/start to begin the protected unlock interaction -> Receive 200 indicating the five-second hold timer has started -> POST /api/unblock/confirm after holding for the required duration -> Receive 200 confirming monitoring was disabled and the app is unlocked
POST /api/unblock/start -> Receive 200 -> POST /api/unblock/cancel before the five-second threshold -> Receive 200 confirming the unlock attempt was aborted and restrictions remain active
POST /api/unblock/confirm without completing the required hold duration -> Receive 403 or 409 rejecting the unlock attempt -> GET /api/blocking/status to confirm restrictions are still enforced

features.name: Restricted App Management
features.description: Allows users to add, update, and remove application packages to restrict their usage time.

features.name: App Usage Monitoring
features.description: Monitors active application usage using UsageStatsManager and Accessibility Service to detect when a restricted app is in the foreground.

features.name: Blocking Overlay Screen
features.description: Displays a system overlay window (BlockOverlayService) over restricted applications once their daily time limit is reached.

features.name: Persistent Logging
features.description: Logs critical actions such as permission changes, restrictions added/removed, and overlay events.

features.name: Permissions Verification
features.description: Requests and verifies crucial Android permissions including Overlay, Usage Stats, Accessibility, Notification, and Battery Optimization.

features.name: Hardened Unblocking
features.description: Implements a protected 5-second long press mechanism (cancelAllWithFiveSecondHold) as the only way to disable monitoring and unlock restricted apps.
